summary: Webb Mountain (lower), Jefferson County: a 1934 sidehill lookout, removed or destroyed in 1966; timbers and a foundation remain in 2015-2016 photos.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 10-foot pole tower (firelookout.com); 2-story slant-walled cabin with garage (firetower.org); sources differ on which structure stood on the sidehill
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1966; timbers and one foundation remain at the sidehill site in photos dated 2015 and 2016.
facts.agency: Washington State Division of Forestry / DNR (builder); U.S. Forest Service listed as administrator on firetower.org

visit.trail_note: Willhite gives directions north of Hoodsport and a parking area at the edge of a clear-cut near the National Forest boundary; a short walk follows.

events.note: Sidehill lookout built by the Washington Division of Forestry; cab set on a pole tower up a ramp of poles.
Per firelookout.com, a two-story slant-walled cabin was constructed on the summit by 1939.
Firetower.org says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed; the index says Removed.

corrections.why: Firetower.org register gives N 47.6169 W 123.0242 for this site (US 850); the record's longitude sits about 0.8 km east. Editor to check on a map, since the record may describe a different point.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says a 10-foot pole L-4 tower stood on the sidehill in 1934 and a two-story slant-walled cabin was built on the summit by 1939. Firetower.org says the slant-walled cabin was built on the sidehill in 1934. The story reports both and does not choose.
Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1966; firetower.org says removed in 1966; the Washington Lookouts index says Removed. All agree on 1966.
Firetower.org gives 2,775 ft and firelookout.com gives 2773 ft; Willhite gives 1,880 ft for the lower site. Not resolved, and elevation is not used in the story.

Washington Lookouts lists the Department of Natural Resources; firelookout.com lists Washington State Division of Forestry/DNR; firetower.org lists the U.S. Forest Service as administrator in Olympic National Forest. Willhite says the site lies just outside the National Forest boundary.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on what stood on the sidehill and when the slant-walled cabin went up (firelookout.com vs firetower.org); the story reports both. Brief coordinates (47.6175, -123.0134) differ from firetower.org (47.6169, -123.0242) by about 0.8 km; firelookout.com's '3 miles SW of Quilcene' does not fit either point and is not used. Willhite's page title says 'Original Location', which may imply a move; no source says the lookout moved, so none is claimed. Geocaching GC7KR65 (a search snippet, not read) describes a former site of the original lookout; not used. Public access is not established; the access key is left out. Reads used: 4 fetches; WebSearch used twice.
